_comment: Flash 1 (issue #27, patches/ff_counter/): read the patch's counter block
plus the context the bench procedure asks for.
patches/ff_counter/test/procedure.md sections 1-4 is the full procedure;
this file is only the variable list it needs.
The three addresses come from patches/ff_counter/patch.json build.ram
(0x7FFB00, 0x100 B, the block re/findings/ram.md section 8.1 recommends):
+0x00 u32 ff_ticks     activations of task_100ms since power-up
+0x04 u16 ff_alive     0xFC01 = 64513 once our code has run
+0x06 u16 ff_reserved  always 0
READ THEM OUT OF patch.json, not out of this file, the day the block moves;
`med9log.py log --patch patches/ff_counter/patch.json` does exactly that
and overrides the three addresses below.
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session logging/sessions/flash1_counter.json \
--patch patches/ff_counter/patch.json --bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 70 \
-o logs/2026-xx-xx_flash1.csv
Checks, in order (procedure.md section 2), with the rates CORRECTED
2026-09-16 from brief C4 (re/findings/scheduler.md sections 11-12,
agent/C4, being merged):
1. ff_alive == 64513.  If it is 0, DO NOT conclude the flash failed:
the hook sits in task_100ms (0x1205A0), which is a SET B task, and
the firmware runs set A unless 0x11DA64 switches to set B
(0x7FEB5E != 0).  Check raster_setA_10ms_count first: if that one is
counting and the set-B ones are frozen, set A is live and our hook
is simply never called.  Only if set B is counting and ff_alive is
still 0 did the hook or the flash write fail.
2. ff_ticks rises monotonically; a single sample can tear in its low
byte, so fit a line over many samples rather than trusting two.
3. task_100ms (0x1205A0) is a 10 ms task, NOT 100 ms: the expected
slope is about 100 counts/s, and ff_ticks must track
raster_setB_10ms_count 1:1.  (Brief C3 first wrote 10/s here from
scheduler.md section 5.4; C4 measured 1 ms = 3508 Time Base ticks of
285 ns and corrected every raster period.)  Expect every rate about
0.25 % LOW, because the OS truncates the 285.714 ns tick to 285 ns.
4. after a power cycle ff_ticks restarts near 0 and ff_alive is 0xFC01.
Record the same variables on the STOCK image first: that baseline and the
Flash-1 log are what tools/logcmp.py compares with
patches/ff_counter/test/tolerance.json.

vars.name: ff_reserved
vars.notes: always 0; a non-zero value means something else writes the block

vars.name: raster_setA_10ms_count
vars.notes: set A 10 ms epilogue. If THIS one moves and the set-B ones do not, our hook is in the task set that is not running -- see check 1

vars.name: raster_setB_10ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
vars.notes: set B 10 ms epilogue (0x120570), the stock counter of the very task our hook sits in: ff_ticks must track it 1:1, about +100/s

vars.name: raster_setA_1ms_count
vars.notes: set A 1 ms epilogue; +1000/s if set A is live

vars.name: raster_setB_1ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
vars.notes: set B 1 ms epilogue (0x11EBDC); +1000/s, the time reference

vars.name: raster_setB_2ms_count
vars.source: re/symbols.csv (C3, address+width); period from scheduler.md sections 11-12 (C4)
